end.summary:
Discussed Bishnoi, sacred groves and Chipko as nature-protecting traditions.
Compared soil loss on tree-covered and bare hills.
Explored neem leaves, baoris, rainwater harvesting and evaporation.
Teach-back was not passed; the belief that traditions teach science was not corrected after last seen.
end.parentNote: Dev practised naming traditional practices and connecting them with protecting trees, soil, water and animals. They used the idea that roots hold soil and suggested a bird-water bowl for a balcony. Dev mixed up how traditional knowledge connects with science, and this was not corrected after it appeared last. At home, ask Dev to explain one practice using: “What does it protect?” and “How can science explain it?”
